dialogue.speaker: Barista
dialogue.en: Good afternoon! What can I get you?

dialogue.speaker: Cliente
dialogue.es: Buenas tardes. Un café americano grande, por favor.
dialogue.en: Good afternoon. A large americano, please.

dialogue.speaker: Cliente
dialogue.es: Sí, una concha, por favor. ¿Cuánto es?
dialogue.en: Yes, a concha, please. How much is it?

dialogue.speaker: Barista
dialogue.es: Sí, claro. Ahorita le paso la terminal.
dialogue.en: Yes, of course. I'll bring you the card machine right away.

notes_en: The americano is 55 pesos and the concha is 30, so 85 in total. 'Ahorita' is very Mexican for 'right away'.

title_en: Asking for the check and paying cash

dialogue.speaker: Mesero
dialogue.en: Shall I bring you the check?

dialogue.speaker: Mesero
dialogue.es: Aquí tiene. Fueron dos cafés de olla y un pan de elote. Son ciento diez pesos.
dialogue.en: Here you go. It was two cafés de olla and a corn cake. It's one hundred ten pesos.

dialogue.speaker: Cliente
dialogue.es: Voy a pagar en efectivo. Aquí tiene, doscientos.
dialogue.en: I'm going to pay in cash. Here you go, two hundred.

dialogue.speaker: Mesero
dialogue.es: Muy bien. Su cambio: noventa pesos. Gracias, ¡vuelva pronto!
dialogue.en: Very good. Your change: ninety pesos. Thanks, come back soon!

notes_en: Each café de olla is 35 pesos and the corn cake is 40. Mexicans often use the preterite 'fueron' when reading back what you ordered.

dialogue.speaker: Taquero
dialogue.en: What will you have, young man?

dialogue.speaker: Cliente
dialogue.es: Me da dos de pastor y uno de suadero, por favor.
dialogue.en: Can I have two al pastor and one suadero, please.

dialogue.speaker: Cliente
dialogue.es: Un agua de horchata chica. ¿Cuánto es?
dialogue.en: A small horchata. How much is it?

dialogue.speaker: Taquero
dialogue.en: Twenty-six in change. Enjoy your meal!

notes_en: Tacos are 18 pesos each and the small horchata is 20: 54 + 20 = 74. 'Con todo' means with onion and cilantro.
